summary.text: 看 is traditionally analyzed as a hand above an eye, shading it to gaze into the distance. This received interpretation is not confirmed by a securely dated early inscription.

formation.text: A semantic compound in the received Shuowen analysis: 手 and 目 combine in the image of a hand shading the eyes while gazing. The account describes the construction but does not confirm it from a securely dated early form.

components.text: 手 depicts the hand above 目 in the traditional gaze-shading interpretation.
目 depicts the eye below 手 in the traditional interpretation.

history.text: The received Shuowen analysis places 手 above 目 and records an alternate graph, 𥉏, written with 倝 as a phonetic. The alternate’s date and graphic relationship to 看 are unresolved; no sequence of graphic change or corruption between the forms is established.

uncertainties.text: The hand-shading interpretation is not confirmed by a securely dated early inscription. The earliest written attestation of 看 and the date of 𥉏 remain unresolved.

evidence.text: Shielding one's eyes 目 with a hand 手 to look to the distance
Depicts putting a hand (手) over the eyes (目) and looking (看) into the distance.
睎也。从手下目。

Ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 手 (“hand”) + 目 (“eye”) – to put a hand above eyes to gaze afar.
STEDT compares it to Proto-Tibeto-Burman *ka(n/ŋ) (“to know; to see”).
Also compare Tibetan མཁན་པོ (mkhan po, “professor; abbot”) (Schuessler, 2007).
睎也。从手下目。

evidence.field: 說文解字 / 字源及釋義
evidence.text: The entry reproduces 說文: “睎也。从手下目。𥉏，看或从倝。” It explains 看 as a semantic compound: transformed 手 above 目, “using the hand to shade the eyes and look into the distance.” The same entry records the later meanings ‘visit,’ ‘watch/look at,’ ‘read,’ ‘observe,’ ‘consider,’ and ‘guard/tend’ under separate readings kān and kàn. These are dictionary-attested uses, not a demonstrated chronological chain.
evidence.title: 看 kàn、kān - 漢典

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: No verified oracle-bone, bronze, or dated Warring States form for 看 was retrieved. The checked sources establish the received Shuowen analysis, not a securely observed chronology of graphic development or possible corruption.

The exact oldest written attestation of the graph and of the spoken senses ‘look,’ ‘guard/watch,’ and ‘visit’ remains unestablished. Dictionary citations from transmitted texts are examples, not a complete dated corpus history.

The link from the concrete hand-above-eye image to broader ‘look/see,’ then to ‘visit,’ ‘read,’ ‘consider,’ ‘guard,’ and ‘tend’ is not established as a dated semantic sequence. Keep the usages distinct until primary textual evidence supports links.

Shuowen records a variant written with 倝 as phonetic (𥉏); no evidence gathered here dates that form or establishes corruption between it and 看. The semantic account of 看 should not be conflated with the phonetic analysis of the variant.

No proposed sound component is supported by the consulted evidence: the dossier’s unverified 龵 decomposition is not evidence of a historical phonetic role. Current readings for 手/目 cannot prove ancient sound relation. No reconstruction comparison was asserted; the local Baxter–Sagart TSV was absent from the checkout.

Official Unihan per-character pages for 看, 手, and 目 were attempted and inaccessible. Local rows checked: pipeline/data/unihan-kmandarin-hsk1.tsv lines 277 (看 kàn) and 192 (手 shǒu); no 目 row. The official lookup documentation page was accessible, but cannot serve as a character-specific reading citation.

The local project search produced a large truncated output when scanning broadly for 看; only the targeted Unihan rows were subsequently used. No full source mirror or local extract recommendation is made: reuse terms for recurrent dictionaries were not assessed and the character-specific pages suffice for concise paraphrase.

No character-specific Xiaoxuetang result or image was retrievable, so there is no justified direct glyph image candidate to propose. The Shuowen page's image links were attempted but failed with cache-miss fetch errors; do not use them as available direct image URLs.

No verified oracle-bone, bronze, or securely dated Warring States form for 看 was found in this external pass. The Shuowen account is a transmitted historical analysis, not confirmation of the visual structure of a pre-Qin artifact.
The alternate graph 𥉏 is reported as a form written with 倝 phonetic; its date, graphic relationship to 看, and any possible corruption history remain unresolved.

Commons’ page identifies the image as Shuowen seal style and lists a Sinica image as its source, but the linked Sinica character-specific page could not be opened; the exact claimed source image was therefore not independently compared. The image is usable only with a narrow label such as ‘Shuowen seal-style form (digital drawing),’ not as a dated inscription.
No directly inspected, securely dated oracle-bone, bronze, or Warring States form was established. The Commons file's alternate-script links and ZDIC catalogue are leads, not date verification.
The alternate 𥉏 is described in the received Shuowen entry as using 倝 phonetic, but its date and graphic relationship to 看, including any corruption proposal, remain unresolved.
Semantic glosses and transmitted text examples establish several uses but not the earliest occurrence of the spoken word or a dated chain connecting gaze/look, visit, read, consider, tend, and guard.

Official Unihan character-specific readings pages for 看, 手, and 目 were inaccessible. Exact local rows were supplied and checked: kàn, shǒu, mù. Their upstream click-through content could not be verified.

The Baxter–Sagart readings were checked against exact harness-provided local rows, including both 看 readings and each proposed component; no fetched official upstream page for the local TSV was verified. The reconstruction comparison supplies no support for 手 or 目 as phonetic components. No sound role is inferred from modern pronunciations.
No tracked extract recommendation is made: the Commons file itself is a verified individual asset with stated CC0 terms, while bulk reuse terms and a versioned dataset extract were not established.

No visual pixel inspection was performed in this research stage. The Commons description and provenance identify the asset as a Shuowen seal-style digital drawing; the harness or visual reviewer should inspect rendered pixels before final selection.
The exact Sinica 27.770B character page was not retrievable, so its label, dating details, and direct CC0 glyph asset could not be checked. Do not substitute a guessed Xiaoxuetang image URL.
No verified oracle-bone, bronze, or securely dated Warring States form for 看 was retrieved. Available form catalogues show/describe received Shuowen or seal-style forms, not an artifact chronology.

The Ministry of Education dictionary supports 𥉏 as a later regularized form of the Shuowen alternate from 倝. It does not date that regularization or establish a continuous graphic path or corruption sequence.

The Commons page states the exact direct SVG URL and licensing, but both the direct image open and exact imageinfo API request failed through the web tool; no API metadata beyond the inspected Commons description page was verified.
